chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, by a chain of his, said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about the one who has an illness in his forehead, not being able to perform Sajdah upon it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should place his chin upon the ground.'
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: 'They are falling down upon their chins in Sajdah.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they cannot place their forehead on the ground during prayer due to illness?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a flexible legal precedent for Sajdah by citing the Quranic phrase 'falling upon their chins' (17:107), thereby validating chin-prostration as a valid alternative when forehead contact is impeded. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (Yusr) in worship, demonstrating how linguistic nuances in the Quran are utilized to derive practical fiqh rulings for those with physical ailments.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, by a chain of his, said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the one who has an illness in his forehead, not being able upon performing Sajdah upon it. Heasws said: ‘He should place his chin upon the ground.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [17:107] they are falling down upon their chins in Sajdah’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from through the chain of his narrators has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of one on whose forehead there is something because of which he is not able to perform Sajdah (prostration) on it. He (the Imam) said, ‘He places his chin on the ground;
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, “They fall down on their chins prostrating.’”” [17:107]
